description.narrative: Increased use of a broad range of quality financial services provided by a stable and competitive financial system in a way which benefits the livelihoods of underserved lower income groups

The Financial Sector Deepening Program (FSD) is a multi-donor programme operating in Kenya through a trust association form. FSD was created to facilitate the development of the financial sector and to increase the access for poor people to financial services in Kenya.

The Financial Sector Deepening Program (FSD) is a multi-donor programme operating in Kenya through a trust association form. FSD was created to facilitate the development of the financial sector and to increase the access for poor people to financial services in Kenya.

Impact Level Results: 1. Growth in inclusion has allowed households to manage their lives better, reducing vulnerability to shocks, allowing better smoothing of consumption and benefits will accrue to non-poor households initially with emergence of finance-enabled products. 2. There is a radical change in financial access landscape but no significant improvement in people’s livelihoods with real economy performing with moderate economic growth and no transformational impact that was once hoped - a finding in Kenya that mirrors global experience. Outcome level Results: 1. Percentage of lower income adults financially excluded stood at 25.2% (male: 24.5; Female: 25.9%) compared to 33.3% in 2013. 2. Access to finance for women has risen sharply with formal inclusion rising to 71.2% in 2016 and the gap with men, 14% in 2009, has now shrunk to 8.5%. If informal finance is included the gap reduces further – 18.6% of women are excluded compared with 16.2% of men. For low-income adults, the difference in access is smaller – 25.9% (women) versus 24.5% (men). 3. While exclusion for youth (23%) is higher than for the overall population (17%), there have been noticeable improvements. For example, 76.9% of low income youth now have formal access compared with 62% in 2014. Output level Results: 1. Overall financial system, the efficiency and affordability of services has improved. Some aspects of the SME finance system, for example the growth of credit reference bureaux, has improved. 2. Knowledge products from FSDK appear to have contributed to change in both the private sector (new services) and public sector (national policies).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
